main_body: Stone column: a long grey shaft (rows 16-40) with a wider rounded-corner cap at the top (rows 8-15) and a matching plinth at the bottom (rows 40-47).
top_band: Light grey cap top at rows 9-12 (L 176-203, with a brighter L 203 edge at row 12), clearly lighter than the shaft (L 150). It sits above a darker 2-row cap front (rows 13-14).
evidence: In the middle column the cap runs: outline row 8, light top rows 9-11, brighter front-edge line at row 12, darker front rows 13-14 (L 150 at x=8, L 124 at x=10), outline row 15, then the shaft at L 150 (rows 17-39). The cap is wider than the shaft and has clipped, rounded corners. It reads as a plate with 4 light rows against 2 front rows, not a thin rim or a straight flat band. The base plinth repeats the same top-then-front structure. This passes, but only narrowly, because the cap top is a boxy plate and not a true ellipse.

style.evidence: The piece has only 8 distinct colours and 8 per tile, against 38-40 colours and 17-20 per tile in the references. Every dark edge pixel is neutral (100%), so the outline is a uniform grey-black sticker line and not a tint of the neighbouring material. The shaft is a smooth horizontal gradient of 3-4 flat grey bands with no grain, chips, cracks or per-stone shading. It carries far less information than the stall and well, and looks thinner and flatter next to them.
